answer_1.quote: Specifically, we believe that there exist gaps between discrete codec models and speech language models... By judiciously reducing information within the first-layer quantizer, employing text (which inherently carries less information compared to speech) to generate first Codec with lower information content can be more easy... For downstream speech language models, we utilized the LibriTTS training set to train zero-shot text-to-speech models.

answer_2.quote: Automatic metrics. For objective evaluation of our codec models, we employ the UTMOS automatic Mean Opinion Score (MOS) prediction system... we also adopt the metrics from speech enhancement fields, such as the PESQ, STOI, and the F1 score for voiced/unvoiced classification (V/UV F1)... To evaluate speaker similarity (SPK) between the original prompt and synthesized speech, we employ WavLM-TDNN... For assessing automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance, we conduct ASR on the generated audio and calculate the word error rate (WER) compared to the original transcriptions.

answer_4.quote: We conduct the MOS (mean opinion score) evaluation on the Librispeech test set to measure the audio naturalness via crowdsourcing in zero-shot TTS experiments... In addition, we also conducted corresponding subjective CMOS tests.
answer_4.guideline: Measure audio naturalness for MOS and compare audio quality and similarity for CMOS.
